quotes: SPRYCEL (dasatinib) is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with
newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+) chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) in chronic phase.
Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) with resistance or intolerance to prior therapy.
Severe thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, and anemia may occur.
Use caution if used concomitantly with medications that inhibit platelet function or anticoagulants.
Fluid retention, sometimes severe, including pleural effusions.
SPRYCEL may increase the risk of developing PAH which may be reversible on discontinuation.
Use SPRYCEL with caution in patients who have or may develop prolongation of the QT interval.
Individual cases of severe mucocutaneous dermatologic reactions have been reported.
Can cause fetal harm.
Assess liver function before initiation of treatment and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated.
Avoid the use of concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and grapefruit juice.

analysis.note: Jabbit analysis. Senolytics are drugs meant to clear senescent ('zombie') cells. The best-known are dasatinib plus quercetin (D+Q) and fisetin. In mice, D+Q increased post-treatment survival in old animals and fisetin extended median and maximum lifespan. No human trial has measured lifespan. Human trials are small (5 to 75 people): early open-label pilots reported better walking tests and fewer senescent cells; a 60-woman bone trial missed its main goal; a 75-person fisetin knee-arthritis trial posted no difference from placebo; an Oct 2026 phase 2 trial in 31 people with fibrotic MASH met its main goal on liver biopsies, with more side effects on D+Q. Dasatinib is a prescription leukemia drug with serious label warnings; quercetin and fisetin are sold as supplements, which FDA does not approve before sale. Patents on senolytic drugs are held by Mayo Clinic, and several trial authors disclose financial interests.
